title: A family budget that survives school fees, weddings and family needs
summary: With children, parents and big family events, a household budget needs more than a spending limit. It needs a pot for every big cost, planned before the month starts.

sections.heading: Start with what's fixed
sections.body: List the costs that come every month: rent or EMI, school fees, groceries, bills. UPI makes paying effortless, which also makes overspending effortless. Look through your UPI history once a month to see where the money really went.

sections.heading: Give every big cost its own pot
sections.body: Family weddings are major expenses and a common reason households take on debt. Save for them monthly in a recurring deposit, which earns about 6.5% and is protected up to ₹5 lakh by DICGC. With inflation around 5.2%, money left in a savings account at about 2.7% slowly loses value.

sections.heading: Family support and the long run
sections.body: Supporting parents is a widely shared expectation, so give it its own line in the budget instead of taking it from savings each time. For goals ten or more years away, a Nifty 50 index fund SIP has historically averaged about 11% a year with ups and downs, and PPF pays about 7.1% with a 15-year lock-in. Avoid credit card debt at about 42% and money lenders at 60% or more.

example.title: Ananya's month in Bengaluru
example.body: Ananya's household takes home ₹95,000. Rent, school fees and bills take ₹50,000, daily spending ₹25,000, and ₹5,000 goes to her parents. The last ₹15,000 is split before the month starts: ₹6,000 into a recurring deposit for a cousin's wedding next year, ₹6,000 into a Nifty 50 SIP for her children's college, and ₹3,000 into PPF.

takeaway: Decide where every rupee goes before the month starts, and give each big family cost its own pot.

quiz.question: A cousin's wedding is a year away. What's the best way to prepare?
options: Put it on a credit card later
Save a fixed amount monthly in a recurring deposit
Borrow from a money lender when it comes
quiz.why: A recurring deposit earns about 6.5% and is protected by DICGC, while cards cost about 42% and lenders 60% or more.

quiz.question: Inflation is about 5.2%. What happens to money left in a 2.7% savings account?
quiz.why: Prices rise faster than the interest it earns, so it buys a little less each year.

quiz.question: Why give support for your parents its own line in the budget?
options: So it doesn't eat into savings each time it's needed
quiz.why: Planned in advance, family support stops being a surprise that drains your savings.
